Senses.PreferredTarget: to depart while seated or die while standing
Senses.Note: Six exact occurrences from 6 independent works are stored.

Occurrences.Kwic: 坐脫立亡則不無先師意未夢見在
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2004.xml). Book of Serenity: Wansong Xingxiu raises Jiufeng’s rejection of the seated head monk and preserves the verdict that seated departure or standing death is present, but the former master’s intent has not even been dreamed of.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB163.xml). Collected Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guting: Guting Shanjian raises the Jiufeng case and then asks whether Jiufeng had grounds for refusing the head monk despite the displayed death.

Occurrences.Kwic: 坐脫立亡則不無，先師意未夢見在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1444.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng: Zhanran Yuancheng retells the case, then reverses its inherited appraisal and argues that Jiufeng, not the head monk, failed to understand.

Occurrences.Kwic: 坐脫立亡即不無，怎奈未夢見先師意在？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB286.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingning Jing: Yingning Jing cites Jiufeng while warning that impressive motionless dying can still be a Chan sickness rather than proof of the matter at issue.

Occurrences.Kwic: 坐脫立亡則不無，先師意未會在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1435.xml). Extended Record of Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai: Wuyi Yuanlai raises the full Jiufeng case and caps it by criticizing both the head monk’s display and Jiufeng’s severity.

Occurrences.Kwic: 凢學道人百年壽滿坐脫立亡報緣未盡行道偶失
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B27/B27n0152.xml). Recorded Sayings of National Preceptor Yulin: Yulin Tongxiu opens a warning by contrasting dying seated or standing when one’s lifespan is complete with spectacular self-destruction before one’s conditions are exhausted.

Senses.Explanation: To depart while seated or die while standing names a conspicuous death display used as evidence of command at life’s end; Chan masters repeatedly preserve the display while refusing to let it prove understanding by itself. Wansong Xingxiu, Guting Shanjian, Zhanran Yuancheng, Yingning Jing, and Wuyi Yuanlai all work the Jiufeng case: a head monk dies seated after staking his claim on understanding Shishuang, but Jiufeng says that seated departure or standing death does not reach the former master’s intent. Their later verdicts differ—Zhanran turns the criticism back on Jiufeng, while Wuyi faults both sides—but all distinguish the feat from the point being tested. Yulin Tongxiu uses the same paired phrase in a warning about death conduct: dying seated or standing when a lifespan is complete is separated from throwing away life before one’s conditions are exhausted. This confirms that the phrase denotes the observable manner of dying, not awakening or authority automatically. The entry describes a claimed demonstration at death. It neither denies that the feat occurs nor accepts it as sufficient proof of understanding; the corpus explicitly contests that inference.
